page: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server configured with eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs based on the Hopper architecture, providing a total of 637 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by Intel Xeon 8481C processors using the x86_64 architecture, delivering 208 vCPUs across 104 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system includes 1872 GB of system memory, yielding 9.0 GB of RAM per core.

In benchmark testing, this server demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities, achieving a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 166,457.52 and a Passmark CPU score of 120,167.87. Memory bandwidth is highly optimized, with uncached large-block reads reaching 423.79 GB/sec and cached small-block reads peaking at 13,241.56 GB/sec. The platform also excels in specialized tasks, scoring in the top 10% for Geekbench ray tracing and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large language model inference benchmarks show strong performance, processing 5,430.06 tokens per second for 7B model prompts and generating 189.54 tokens per second.

A primary architectural tradeoff of the a3-edgegpu-8g-nolssd is the complete absence of local SSD storage, requiring all data persistence to rely on network-attached storage. This design optimizes the server for workloads where massive parallel GPU compute and high memory capacity are prioritized over local disk I/O. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of eight H100 GPUs and 1872 GB of RAM represents a specialized tier of hardware designed to maximize throughput per node for massive parallel processing, though it carries a high resource footprint.

This server is engineered for large-scale artificial intelligence and machine learning workloads, including LLM training, high-throughput LLM inference, and complex data science pipelines. It is also highly suitable for compute-heavy tasks such as ray tracing, cryptographic processing, and high-performance multi-threaded simulations.

The system is equipped with 1872 GB of RAM, providing 9.0 GB per core, but lacks local SSD storage, requiring network-attached storage for data persistence. In benchmarks, the server delivers top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and LLM inference processing. This hardware profile is optimized for demanding workloads such as large language model training, high-performance simulations, ray tracing, and intensive data science tasks.
